text:
Anna (support): Hey — Customer ACME reports sudden spike of 429s + >250ms median latency since ~06:10 UTC, mostly EU users. They say dashboard shows requests routed to us-east-1 instead of eu-west-1 :eyes:
Sam H (engineer): Thanks. Any example request IDs or client IPs? 429 suggests per-region ratelimit/backpressure.
Anna (support): Provided request IDs: r_3f2a, r_3f2b, r_3f8c. Client IP samples: 81.23.45.67, 88.99.12.5. Also sent their traceroute showing hop into us-east cloud.
Tom N - NetEng: That smells like DNS/GeoIP mismatch or stale ISP cache. Did ACME change their region preference or pin model variants?
Anna (support): They say they didn't change config. They pin model to `redwood-llama-3b` but left routing policy to auto.
Maya (SRE): Can you ask them to run `dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.example` and `dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example` and paste results? Need to compare resolver answers. Also run `dig +trace api.redwood.example`.
Anna (support): Pasted results:
```
# 1.1.1.1 -> 34.120.11.7
# 8.8.8.8 -> 54.3.2.10
```
Sam H (engineer): Different A records from different resolvers — confirms inconsistent view. 34.120.11.7 is eu node, 54.3.2.10 is us node (mapping from our catalog).
Tom N - NetEng: Could be TTL mismatch between authoritative zone and our GeoIP CDN. If authoritative returned low TTL but CDN / authoritative glue had older entries, some ISP caches may hold the US answer. Also EDNS/EDNS-client-subnet could affect geo routing.
Anna (support): ACME reports the user agent `curl/7.68.0` on their webapp gets us-east for many EU clients. They tried `nslookup` and still saw old US IPs.
Maya (SRE): Please ask them to run these repro commands from an impacted client and paste outputs:
```
dig +short api.redwood.example @<their_resolver>
dig +trace api.redwood.example
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example:443:34.120.11.7 https://api.redwood.example/v1/health
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example:443:54.3.2.10 https://api.redwood.example/v1/health
```
Anna (support): They ran `dig +trace` — trace shows delegations to our nameservers, but the glue records at one intermediate ISP still point to the us-east address, TTL reported as 86400 on that path.
Sam H (engineer): 86400 TTL is the problem — an upstream resolver cached the old A for 24h. We recently changed the geo A answer during rollout. Need to identify which upstream resolver is serving the stale answer and ask them to flush or wait.
Tom N - NetEng: Actions I suggest: 1) confirm authoritative zone TTL and that our geo DNS records were updated with low pre-roll TTL before the change, 2) check our NS provider propagation logs, 3) contact the ISP (or advise customer to use 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8) or set short client-side DNS TTL if possible.
Anna (support): ACME is asking for a faster mitigation — users are losing revenue. Any way to force fallback to eu from our side?
Maya (SRE): We can add an HTTP-level routing hint if client includes `X-Region-Hint: eu-west-1` but ACME would need to set that header from their client, which they control. Otherwise we can temporarily relax cross-region rate limits so even routed-to-us-east requests won't 429, but that increases cost and may affect capacity.
Sam H (engineer): Before changing rate limits, let's try to identify the resolvers returning stale records. Anna, can you ask for `dig +short api.redwood.example @81.23.45.67` (their ISP resolver) and the `EDNS Client Subnet` output: `dig +edns=0 @<resolver> +norecurse api.redwood.example`?
Anna (support): Done. Their ISP resolver returns 54.3.2.10 and EDNS-C is empty. ISP confirmed they have a long TTL cached and won't refresh until expiry.
Tom N - NetEng: Ok. Short-term options: 1) Advise ACME to switch to public resolvers (Cloudflare/Google) which already see EU answer, 2) We temporarily widen per-region token buckets so us-east won't 429, 3) Ask our DNS provider to push a forced update/flush if supported. I'll open a ticket with DNS vendor.
DevOps Bot: [deploy] routing/fallback:rate-limit-temporary-adjustment started by Maya at 1791234585
Maya (SRE): I'll start a controlled change to soften the ratelimit for 15 min while DNS converges. Monitoring: latency, 429 rate, egress cost.
Sam H (engineer): Also add a note to docs: when doing geo- DNS switches, pre-warm with low TTL (<=300) and coordinate with major ISPs if possible. This case shows TTL mismatch + ISP cache = cross-region traffic + billing hit.
Anna (support): Communicated back to ACME: suggested immediate workarounds (use 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8, set `X-Region-Hint`, or accept temporary rate-limit softening). They chose to flip to 1.1.1.1 for now and will monitor. :thumbsup:
Tom N - NetEng: Follow-up items: 1) DNS vendor ticket ID DNS-7895, 2) add test to our rollout checklist to verify common public resolvers within 5 minutes, 3) consider lowering authoritative TTL before geo changes.
Maya (SRE): Rolling back the rate-limit change now (15m window ended). Watchdog shows 429s down to baseline.
Anna (support): ACME confirms latency back to normal for most EU users. Closing on our side but leaving DNS-7895 open until vendor confirms flush.
Sam H (engineer): Great. Saving repro commands and notes to the runbook.
Anna (support): Thanks everyone! :heart:
